reason: Reproduced exactly at 1440 on ?v=approach&state=owner-editing. Press +7 on 'Send the invitations': rows 7, bar reads 'Last change: Send the invitations moved 7 days later.', Undo live. Press 'Delete this moment': rows 6, the moment is gone, and the bar STILL names the deleted moment with Undo live and data-empty=false — the delete branch in render-b.js wireOwner (item.remove(); place(measureEl)) neither pushes history nor calls paintUndo, so the bar advertises an undo for a row that no longer exists. Press Undo: rows stay 6, no date changes, and the bar goes data-empty=true with empty text — undo() does 'var last = history.pop()' then 'if (item) { ... }' with no else, so a popped record whose row is gone silently restores nothing, and the following paintUndo() reads the now-empty history and hides the bar, which is indistinguishable from a successful undo. That is the distinct claim of this finding and it is a silent failure of the surface's only reversibility promise, independent of whether delete itself should be undoable. Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs asserts only that delete removes the moment and the measure reflows, and its undo assertions all run on a still-present row; nothing asserts that an undo changes the surface or that the bar never names a moment that is gone. No constraint is touched — the fix is behaviour in render-b.js, no colour, weight, family or architecture change.
sharpenedFix: Aim it at undo()'s own contract, not only at delete-undo (a separate finding owns that). In render-b.js: (1) make undo() peek before it pops — resolve the row for history[history.length-1] first, and only pop when the entry can actually be applied; a stale entry must never be silently consumed. (2) At delete time, prune history of every entry whose id is the deleted row and call paintUndo(root) in the same frame, so the bar never keeps naming a moment that no longer exists (the current fix text's 'leave the bar saying what is still undone' is incoherent for a row that can never return — prune at the source instead). (3) If delete is made reversible, push { kind: 'delete', id, record, index } before item.remove() and teach undo() to re-insert at index and re-place the measure, with bar text 'Last change: <title> was deleted.' — in that case step (2) becomes 'rewrite stale move entries relative to the restored row' rather than pruning. Gate: add to interaction-check.mjs (a) after a delete the bar either names the deletion or is silent, never names the deleted moment's earlier move, and (b) no Undo press may leave row count, dates and bar state all unchanged — i.e. an undo that changes nothing must not clear the bar.
